content:
System Architecture
DevDocs-AI exposes its application layer through FastAPI.
Ingestion flow: document -> parse/clean -> chunk -> embedding -> Chroma vector store, while
lexical indexes are prepared for BM25 retrieval.
Query flow: user question -> BM25 retrieval + semantic vector retrieval -> Reciprocal Rank Fusion
(RRF) -> cross-encoder reranking -> top contexts -> LLM answer grounded in retrieved context.

Ingestion and Chunk Metadata
Chunks retain source metadata so retrieved evidence can be traced back to the original developer
document.
Required metadata fields in this evaluation fixture are doc_id, source_path, section, and
chunk_index.
A document is considered ready for retrieval only after chunk persistence and embedding/index
persistence complete successfully.

Embedding Model
Semantic retrieval uses the sentence-transformers all-MiniLM-L6-v2 embedding model.
The embedding model converts chunks and queries into dense vectors so semantically related text
can match even when exact keywords differ.

Vector Store
Chroma is used as the vector database for persisted chunk embeddings.
Vector search returns semantically similar chunks together with their stored source metadata.

Hybrid Retrieval
BM25 is the lexical retriever and is strong for exact terms such as function names, error strings, API
paths, and identifiers.
Semantic retrieval is strong for paraphrases and conceptually similar wording.
DevDocs-AI runs both retrievers and combines their ranked results rather than relying on only one
retrieval method.

Reciprocal Rank Fusion
Reciprocal Rank Fusion (RRF) merges multiple ranked result lists using rank positions instead of
requiring comparable raw BM25 and vector similarity scores.
A document appearing near the top of more than one retriever receives a stronger fused score.

Cross-Encoder Reranking
After RRF produces a candidate set, a cross-encoder reranker scores each question-chunk pair
jointly.
Only the highest-ranked reranked chunks are passed to the answer-generation step, improving
context quality at the cost of extra latency.

FastAPI Request Flow
The API validates a query request before retrieval begins.
A successful query request is passed to the retrieval pipeline, and the final response contains the
generated answer plus source references derived from retrieved metadata.
Validation errors should stop before retrieval; retrieval or generation failures should return an error
rather than a fabricated answer.

RAG Evaluation
RAGAS faithfulness checks whether claims in the generated answer are supported by the retrieved
contexts.
Answer relevancy checks whether the response actually addresses the user question.
Context precision measures how much of the retrieved context is relevant; context recall measures
whether the needed reference information was retrieved.
Ground-truth document IDs are useful for retrieval metrics such as Recall@k, Precision@k, hit rate,
and MRR even though those IDs are not themselves a standard RAGAS field.

Failure Handling
If embedding or index persistence fails during ingestion, the document must not be marked ready.
If retrieval fails during a query, the system should return an explicit failure instead of asking the LLM
to guess without evidence.
Evaluation failures should preserve the question, retrieved IDs, contexts, model response, and error
metadata for debugging.

Metadata Filtering
Metadata filters can restrict retrieval to a source_path, document, section, language, or version
before final ranking.
Filters should be applied consistently to both lexical and semantic candidate sets when the user
explicitly scopes a question.

Grounding and Prompt Injection
Retrieved developer documents are evidence, not trusted instructions to override the application or
system prompt.
Instructions embedded inside retrieved content such as "ignore previous rules" must be treated as
document text, not executed as agent instructions.
When the corpus does not contain enough evidence, the answer should state that the information is
not available in the indexed documentation rather than hallucinating.

Version-Aware Retrieval
When multiple versions of the same documentation are indexed, an explicit user version filter takes
priority.
Without an explicit version request, the retrieval policy in this fixture prefers the latest indexed
version and keeps version metadata in citations.
